• expected impact of plans and strategy for the acceleration of our data center footprint and our PoP deployment;

• expectations that proceeds from the exercise of stock options in future years will be adversely impacted by the increased mix of restricted stock units and performance stock units versus stock options granted or a decline in our stock price;
We expect our product revenue to continue to grow year over year for the remainder of 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025.
We expect our service revenue to continue to grow year over year for the remainder of 2026.
Our overall gross margin for the full year of 2026 will be impacted by service and product revenue mix and their respective gross margins.

We also expect service gross margin for the full year 2026 to remain relatively consistent with 2025, while continuing expansion of our data center footprint and colocation and cloud hosting capacity to support the growth in our unified SASE and SecOps offerings.
We currently do not expect the U.S. tariffs to have a meaningful impact on our gross margin.

However, changes in trade policy, including increases in tariff rates, changes in customs or tariff classifications, or modifications to tariff exemptions, could adversely affect our gross margin in the future, and we expect any resulting impact would primarily relate to our hardware sales to U.S. customers.
For the full year 2026, we expect our operating margin to increase slightly compared to 2025, benefiting from operating leverage and measured investments.
We expect these and other investments to support long-term revenue growth and market expansion.

In addition, it is important to note that other companies, including companies in our industry, may not use free cash flow, may calculate free cash flow in a different manner than we do or may use other financial measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of free cash flow as a comparative measure.
To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and our actual results, our future financial statements will be affected.
We expect research and development expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the full year 2026 as compared to 2025 as we invest to drive continued innovation in our products and services.

We expect our sales and marketing expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the full year 2026 as compared to 2025 as we continue to invest in our global sales and marketing organization to capture additional market share.

We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the full year 2026 as compared to 2025, primarily to support our growing operations while continuing to leverage scale and efficiencies.
In July 2026, Moody’s upgraded certain of our credit ratings to A3 from Baa1 and changed the outlook to Stable from Positive.
Our S&P ratings remain BBB+ with a Stable outlook.

We expect proceeds from the exercise of stock options in future years to continue to be impacted by the increased mix of restricted stock units and performance stock units versus stock options granted to our employees and to vary based on our stock price.
We expect to continue to increase our data center, PoP, office and warehouse capacity to support growth and the expansion of existing services or introduction of new services.
As we purchase new properties, we will work to incorpo rate these properties into the environmental goals we have established.
We record a liability for inventory purchase commitments in excess of our future demand forecasts consistent with the valuation of our excess and obsolete inventory.
We believe the amount of our inventory and purchase commitments is appropriate for our current and expected customer demand and revenue levels.

Based on current projections, we expect to have sufficient liquidity to meet our operating requirements for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future, including our foreseeable future supply obligations, capital expenditures and share repurchases.

We believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents and cash flow from operations will be sufficient for at least the next 12 months to meet our requirements and plans for cash, including meeting our working capital requirements and capital expenditure requirements.
We expect to make similar decisions in the future.
